meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. I have a client call at 4:40, Hale. Who decided on that zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
The zero stands, on what basis? Your own procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark goes in, and I wasn't. Answer my question, or I'm walking straight to the principal's office from here.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

I'm writing down October 15. Show me the line, the exact words, and the outline itself, Hale. And students change their arguments between an outline and a final draft, so who else has seen these two documents?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn and an apology for entering it before anyone called me, and I want to see the essay line and the October outline you described. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still in her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the documents herself.
What moved her: "his October 15 outline argued cowardice", because it was dated and tied to Owen's own work, so she stopped attacking and started writing it down.
What cost ground: "The zero stands.", because it defended the mark with no basis and pushed her straight to threatening the principal.
Try next time: open by owning in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put the October 15 outline and the misquoted line on the screen so she can read them for herself.
